# The price of prescribed marginals in characteristic-function dependence: phase contact and complete mixability

Alexandr Martinevski · ORCID 0009-0000-4230-4414

Published version: 2026-10-14 · DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23355597

## Abstract

For identical prescribed one-dimensional marginals $F$, we maximize the characteristic-function factorization defect over all couplings and signed frequency vectors. A convex-order and cosine-contact argument produces a scalar phase profile, but we carefully distinguish this upper profile ${\kappa }_{d}(F)$ from the actual coupling optimum ${K}_{d}(F)$. Under specified Fourier log-concavity, spectral-gap and anti-concentration assumptions, equality for all sufficiently large dimensions holds exactly when the absolute-value marginal $|X|$ is completely mixable, i.e. admits a constant-sum coupling.

We obtain finite-dimensional conclusions: the scalar profile is attained for uniform marginals in every $d\ge 3$; for Gaussian marginals it is strictly unattainable in every such dimension. For sums of three and four independent uniform variables (B-spline marginals), attainment begins exactly at dimensions four and five, respectively. We also quantify the asymptotic cost of fixing the marginal law: in the symmetric regular regime, ${C}_{d}-{K}_{d}(F)=\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2d}(Var(X)/(\mathbb{E}|X|{)}^{2}-1)+o({d}^{-1})$. A median-based construction supplies a nonsymmetric lower bound. No universal equality between the scalar profile and the fixed-marginal optimum is claimed.

## Keywords

  * Prescribed marginals
  * Characteristic-function dependence
  * Complete mixability
  * Sharp coupling bounds
  * Uniform and Gaussian marginals
  * B-spline distributions
  * Convex order
  * Fourier log-concavity
  * Extremal dependence
  * Asymptotic coupling gap

## Selected results

  1. Uniform marginals attain the exact phase profile for d≥3; quadratic and cubic B-splines attain it from d=4 and d=5.
  2. Under stated Fourier hypotheses, equality is equivalent to complete mixability of |X|; Gaussian laws have a strict gap.
  3. Without symmetry, a median construction gives K_d(F)≥2−π²Var(X)/(2d(E|X−a|)²)+o(1/d) for a median a.

Technion Israel Institute of Technology

## Abstract

We consider a random walk in a random environment on $\mathbb{Z}^d$Z d under ballisticity condition $(T)$(T). We show the existence of the invariant measure $Q$Q with respect to the environment viewed from the particle for $d=2$d=2 and $d=3$d=3, which disproves a conjecture made in arXiv:1405.6819 regarding the two-dimensional case. We also prove tail estimates for the Radon-Nikodym derivative $dQ/dP$d Q/d P, where $P$P is the original distribution on the environment. Lastly, we provide nearly sharp tail bounds for regeneration times for $d=3$d=3.

dc.description.abstract  | Mixability is a property of a loss which characterizes when constant regret is possible in the game of prediction with expert advice. We show that a key property of mixability generalizes, and the exp and log operations present in the usual theory are not as special as one might have thought. In doing so we introduce a more general notion of φ-mixability where φ is a general entropy (i.e., any convex function on probabilities). We show how a property shared by the convex dual of any such entropy yields a natural algorithm (the minimizer of a regret bound) which, analogous to the classical Aggregating Algorithm, is guaranteed a constant regret when used with φ-mixable losses. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Title: Environment Viewed from the Particle and Slowdown Estimates for Ballistic RWRE on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and $\mathbb{Z}^3$
Authors: Tal Peretz
Date: Tue Apr 26 11:36:53 2022

We consider a random walk in a random environment on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ under Sznitman's ballisticity condition $(T)$. Using techniques from arXiv:1405.6819, we show the existence of the invariant measure $Q$ with respect to the environment viewed from the particle for $d=2$ and $d=3$. This disproves a conjecture made in arXiv:1405.6819 that the invariant measure does not exist in dimension $2$. As a corollary, we prove sharp tail bounds for regeneration times for $d=3$. Finally, we also provide tail estimates for the Radon-Nikodym derivative $dQ/dP$, where $P$ is the original distribution on the environment.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
